title: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Most evolutionary changes at the molecular level are caused by random drift of selectively neutral or nearly neutral mutations, not by positive selection.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: empirical claim: for most sites |N_e s| \lesssim 1, so the fraction of substitutions driven by positive selection \alpha is small; tested with d_N/d_S and McDonald-Kreitman \alpha = 1 - \frac{D_s P_n}{D_n P_s}

fields.label: Context in the nanopub
fields.value: Formal status: not a mathematical statement; an empirical claim about the distribution of fitness effects. King and Jukes (1969) proposed it independently. Genomic estimates of alpha and pervasive linked selection are cited against its strong form (Kern and Hahn 2018).

fields.value: Estimate the proportion of adaptive substitutions (alpha) with McDonald-Kreitman-type tests genome-wide across many species, correcting for slightly deleterious polymorphism and demography.
